<Callout type="warn" title="Coming soon — not yet available">
  District is a platform gamexo knows about, but the integration is not built. There are
  no endpoints, and **no API key can be issued for it**. Attempting to create one is
  refused rather than quietly producing a key that cannot answer.
</Callout>

## What exists today

District appears in a venue's integrations screen as a platform we are working towards,
so a venue can see it is coming. That is the whole of it. Nothing guesses at field
names or endpoint paths: an invented contract would be worse than an empty one,
because it would look finished.

## What is blocking it

District's published integration contract. Once we have it, building the adapter is one
module — the wire format, and nothing else.

Everything underneath is already written and already running for
[Playo](/docs/integrations/third-party/playo): availability, holds, atomic
multi-slot writes, idempotent retries, 15-minute expiry, per-venue scoping, and an
eight-scenario consistency suite. A new adapter inherits all of it without
reimplementing any of it, which is why the estimate is short once the spec lands.

## In the meantime

If District can call our contract rather than dictating one, no waiting is needed. The
[gamexo API](/docs/integrations/gamexo-api) is live today and a venue can issue a key
for it now.

## For the District team

If you are reading this to scope an integration, what we need from you is:

- The endpoints you expect the venue to host, with paths and methods.
- Request and response bodies, including how you signal a business refusal versus a
  transport fault.
- How times are expressed — offset, venue-local, or UTC — and how date and time are
  split, if they are.
- The identifier you will send that is stable across your own retries. That value
  becomes the idempotency key, and it is what stops a dropped response from
  double-selling a court.
- Whether you want a two-phase hold-then-confirm flow, or single-phase confirmed
  bookings.

Send that to your gamexo contact and the adapter follows.
